name: Mexico City
summary: Mexico City stands on the drained bed of a highland lake, at about 2,240 metres, directly on top of the Aztec island-capital of Tenochtitlan. Founded by the Mexica in 1325 where an eagle perched on a cactus — the omen now stamped on the national flag — it was besieged and razed by Hernán Cortés in 1521 and rebuilt as the capital of New Spain. It is the largest Spanish-speaking city on Earth and, sinking slowly back into its old lakebed, both endlessly troubled by water and impossible to move.

events.title: Tenochtitlan is founded
events.body: The Mexica found Tenochtitlan on an island in Lake Texcoco, guided by the eagle-and-cactus omen.

events.title: The first tlatoani
events.body: Acamapichtli becomes the first tlatoani (ruler) of the Mexica.

events.title: The Triple Alliance
events.body: The Aztec Triple Alliance is forged; the empire begins to expand.

events.title: Dykes against the lake
events.body: Under Moctezuma I the city builds a great dyke and aqueducts against flooding.

events.title: The Templo Mayor dedicated
events.body: The rebuilt Templo Mayor is dedicated with mass sacrificial rites.

events.title: Moctezuma II at the height
events.body: Moctezuma II ascends the throne at the empire’s height.

events.title: Cortés reaches Tenochtitlan
events.body: Hernán Cortés reaches Tenochtitlan and takes Moctezuma hostage.

events.title: The Sad Night
events.body: The “Sad Night”: the Mexica drive the Spanish from the city with heavy losses.

events.title: The fall of Tenochtitlan
events.body: After a brutal siege and smallpox, Tenochtitlan falls; Cortés founds Mexico City on the ruins.

events.title: The Virgin of Guadalupe
events.body: Our Lady of Guadalupe is said to appear to Juan Diego on Tepeyac hill.

events.title: Capital of New Spain
events.body: Mexico City becomes the capital of the Viceroyalty of New Spain.

events.title: The Royal University
events.body: The Royal University of Mexico is founded, among the first in the Americas.

events.title: The great flood of 1629
events.body: A catastrophic flood submerges the city for years, prompting vast drainage works.

events.title: The maize riots
events.body: Riots over maize shortages burn the viceroy’s palace on the Zócalo.

events.title: The Cry of Dolores
events.body: Father Hidalgo’s “Cry of Dolores” launches the war of independence.

events.title: Independence won
events.body: Independence is won; Mexico City becomes capital of a new nation.

events.title: The Niños Héroes
events.body: US troops storm Chapultepec Castle; the young cadets die as the Niños Héroes.

events.title: Maximilian’s empire
events.body: The French install the Habsburg Maximilian as emperor in Mexico City.

events.title: The republic restored
events.body: Maximilian is overthrown and executed; the republic is restored under Juárez.

events.title: The Porfiriato begins
events.body: Porfirio Díaz begins decades of rule, modernising and beautifying the capital.

events.title: The Revolution erupts
events.body: The Mexican Revolution erupts against the Díaz dictatorship.

events.title: The Ten Tragic Days
events.body: The “Ten Tragic Days” of street fighting devastate central Mexico City.

events.title: The founding of the PRI
events.body: The party that will rule for 71 years (later the PRI) is founded.

events.title: The Palace of Fine Arts
events.body: The Palace of Fine Arts opens, filling with murals by Rivera and his rivals.

events.title: The Tlatelolco massacre
events.body: Troops massacre student protesters at Tlatelolco days before the Olympics.

events.title: The 1968 Olympics
events.body: Mexico City hosts the Summer Olympics, the first in Latin America.

events.title: The Templo Mayor rediscovered
events.body: Electrical workers rediscover the buried Templo Mayor beneath the centre.

events.title: The 1985 earthquake
events.body: A magnitude-8 earthquake kills thousands and flattens whole districts.

events.title: The H1N1 pandemic
events.body: The H1N1 flu pandemic first alarms the world from Mexico City.

events.title: CDMX is born
events.body: The Federal District becomes the autonomous entity of Mexico City (CDMX).

events.title: The 2017 earthquake
events.body: Another major earthquake — 32 years to the day after 1985 — strikes the city.

places.name: Templo Mayor / Zócalo
places.note: The great Aztec temple and the vast main square built over it.

places.name: Chapultepec
places.note: The ancient forested hill and its castle, west of the centre.

places.name: Basilica of Guadalupe
places.note: On Tepeyac hill, where the Virgin is said to have appeared in 1531.

places.name: Palace of Fine Arts
places.note: The marble concert hall (1934), filled with murals by Rivera and rivals.

places.name: Tlatelolco
places.note: Aztec sister-city and market; site of the 1968 massacre.

caveats: This timeline is compiled from general reference works — listed under Sources — rather than an event-by-event archive of primary documents, as the Mumbai timeline is. Treat it as a reliable outline, not a citation of record.
Dates for the earliest, legendary events are traditional rather than documented.

dynasties.note: The ruling lines of the city, from the Mexica tlatoque to the makers of modern Mexico.

list.name: The Mexica tlatoque
list.summary: The line of rulers (tlatoque) from Acamapichtli (c. 1375) through Moctezuma I and II to Cuauhtémoc, who built and led an empire from Tenochtitlan until the Spanish conquest ended it.

list.legacy: Mexico City and the pattern of New Spain
list.name: Hernán Cortés & the conquistadors
list.summary: Cortés destroyed Tenochtitlan in 1521 and founded Mexico City over it, becoming the first Marqués del Valle de Oaxaca and setting the pattern of colonial New Spain.

list.legacy: The wealth of New Spain — and the drive to independence
list.name: The criollo elite
list.summary: American-born Spanish families grew immensely wealthy on silver mining and vast estates during three centuries as capital of New Spain, and ultimately led the drive to independence against the Crown.

list.legacy: The modern nation, shaped from its capital
list.name: Revolutionary leaders
list.summary: From Miguel Hidalgo’s 1810 cry for independence and Benito Juárez’s reforms to Madero, Zapata and Villa in the Revolution, these figures reshaped the nation from and around its capital.
